clue.text: Furtive person hiding head of woodwork's stand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the head letter is hidden away, so it drops out of sight and out of the word

blocks.note: a weasel is a sly, sneaky person
the head, or first letter, of woodwork

explanation.surface: A sneaky character conceals the best bit of a piece of carpentry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden frame that holds up a painting or blackboard, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Stunt ace departs in Dodge

indicators.note: the first pair of letters goes inside the word for dodge

blocks.note: to dodge something is to escape it
A is the card abbreviation for ace
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A daredevil pilot pulls a stunt by slipping away in a Dodge car.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit, much like a stunt.

clue.text: Moves text in lists below second chapter

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming below means being written after the earlier pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
C is the abbreviation for chapter
rolls are official lists of names

explanation.surface: Someone shifts words around in lists that follow the second chapter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts the lists after the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: On a screen, to scroll is to move the displayed text up or down, a verb matching 'moves'.

clue.text: Might Cook use this singer with Dud?

blocks.note: a lemon is a dud, something that fails to work
a grass is an informer, one who sings to the police

explanation.surface: Would comedian Peter Cook have used this singer alongside his partner Dud?
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Cook's comedy partner was Dudley Moore, 'Dud', but here Cook is any cook and Dud a failure. The singer comes first in the clue but second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemongrass is a fragrant grass used as a herb, so a cook might well use it.

clue.text: Histrionic period in Lens?

indicators.note: the period sits inside the word for lens

blocks.note: an optic is a lens in an optical instrument
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dramatic phase in the French town of Lens?
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, Lens looks like the town in northern France; here it is just a lens.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic behaviour is extravagantly theatrical, as histrionic behaviour is overly dramatic.

clue.text: Designer whose work gets her down in a way?

definitions.text: Designer whose work gets her down in a way?

blocks.clueFragment: Designer whose work gets her down
blocks.note: surface reading: a designer depressed by her job
setter's reading: the artist's work is put down on a way, the walkway beside a road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets her down' suggests depression; really the work is laid down on the ground of a walkway, drawn in chalk.
explanation.definitionFit: This street artist chalks pictures onto paving stones, so the work lies flat on a footway.

clue.text: Starters of rendang and nasi goreng gave someone a buzz

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the following words

blocks.note: first letters of rendang, and, nasi, goreng

explanation.surface: Starters of Malaysian beef curry and fried rice prompted someone to call.
explanation.walkthrough: Rendang and nasi goreng are Southeast Asian dishes; 'starters' suits a menu but means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a buzz is informal for phoning them, the past tense matching 'rang'.

clue.text: Ultimately just grounds for rebellion

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: the final letter of just
grounds for something are its reason

explanation.surface: In the end there is fair cause for revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, an act of rebellion against the state.

clue.text: Smart girl ignored by vacuous enemy

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is emptied and only its outer letters stay

blocks.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
enemy with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A clever young woman is snubbed by an empty-headed foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutey is an attractive or charming young woman, and smart can mean stylish and good-looking.

clue.text: No Ginger Creams? Ridiculously alarmist!

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is done absurdly, so the letters come out in a crazy new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A shopper panics on finding the biscuit tin has run out of ginger creams.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger creams are a British sandwich biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaremongering is spreading needless fear, the adjective sense matching alarmist.

clue.text: No base once in defective ice cream pot

indicators.note: no says that the base is taken away from the fodder
once limits the removal to a single occurrence, though two are available
something defective is faulty, so the letters are put together wrongly

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
taken as written

explanation.surface: Faulty ice cream in a tub with no bottom spills out.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Es leaves, which is why 'once' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramic is an article of fired clay, such as a pot, the noun use of the word.

clue.text: Small amount on French wine? Price on screen, perhaps

blocks.note: vin is French for wine
a cent is a small coin or sum

explanation.surface: A small sum added to a French wine's cost, shown on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the small amount after the wine. Vincent Price was a Hollywood horror actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent is the first name of the film star Price, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Maybe Hannah and Linda cycling in west side of Panama City

indicators.note: the west side of a word written across is its leftmost, first letter
cycling moves letters round in a loop, the last one coming to the front

blocks.note: first letter of Panama
taken as written
Rome is a capital city

explanation.surface: Two women ride bikes around the western edge of Panama City.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama City is the capital of Panama, but the clue splits it: Panama gives one letter, City another word. Linda's last letter goes to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah reads the same backwards as forwards, making it an example of a palindrome.

clue.text: Notice questionable faculty Yale's opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: extrasensory perception, a sixth sense whose existence is doubtful
first letter of Yale

explanation.surface: Spot the dubious professors at the start of term at Yale.
explanation.walkthrough: Faculty suggests university staff, fitting Yale; here it is a mental power.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, as to notice something is to see it.

clue.text: Kitten said to be mad for high-protein regimen

indicators.note: being mad means being deranged, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A kitten is said to be crazy about a meaty diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atkins diet is a low-carbohydrate eating plan heavy in protein, devised by Dr Robert Atkins.

clue.text: Sensitive, or behaving intolerantly?

blocks.note: first meaning: showing fine judgement and taste
second meaning: treating people unfairly because of prejudice

explanation.walkthrough: The word has a flattering sense and an ugly one.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning palate is discriminating, while unfair treatment of groups is discriminating against them.

clue.text: Guardiola possibly welcoming runs by a left-winger, fit

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the nickname holds the next letter

blocks.note: Pep Guardiola is the football manager; possibly flags this as one Pep among others
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
a Red is a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: The Manchester City manager lets in goals from a left winger who is fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Left-winger sounds like a football position; it is a political radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fit for something can mean ready for it, as prepared means ready.

clue.text: Wasting easy opportunity in need of a childminder

blocks.note: first meaning: failing to score from a sitter, an easy chance
second meaning: lacking a babysitter

explanation.walkthrough: A sitter is football slang for a chance that should never be missed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sporting idiom for blowing a simple chance, and literally means lacking a babysitter.

clue.text: Where meter can be read upside down?

blocks.note: first meaning: in poetry, where metrical rhythm is found
second meaning: turned the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: Meter suggests a gas or electricity meter; it is poetic metre, the US spelling. The first reading splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means reversed or inverted in position, so upside down; 'in verse' is where metre lives.

clue.text: Star regularly receiving warmth on stage at the end here?

definitions.text: Star regularly receiving warmth on stage at the end here?

indicators.note: regularly keeps every other letter of the word
receiving means taking in, so the selected letters hold the word for warmth
at the end points to the final letter of the word before

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of star
heat is warmth
final letter of stage

explanation.surface: A star, warmly received on stage at the curtain call, is in this building.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a theatre is where a star gets a warm reception on stage at the end of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the playhouse where performers take their applause on stage after the show.

clue.text: Misleading conversation in US dance

blocks.note: first meaning: deceptive or glib talk, US slang
second meaning: a lively swing dance from America

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins the two meanings, so it should not be read as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang jive is talk meant to deceive, and it is also a fast jazz dance of the 1940s.

clue.text: Mixture doctor leaves with soft drink

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a jumble is a mixture
MB is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A doctor walks out, leaving a cordial mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' looks like a single phrase, but soft is the wordplay and drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, such as the bourbon and mint julep of the American South.

clue.text: Drop off drunk poet and elegist I must keep away from

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are scrambled
keeping away means being absent, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy poet and a writer of laments: I must avoid them to nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for falling asleep, which is what getting to sleep means.

clue.text: Plot having top of peaty soil mostly

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: first letter of peaty
land is soil or ground

explanation.surface: A garden plot whose top layer is mostly peat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like ground, but it is a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or secret design, and a plan is likewise a scheme.

clue.text: Some deplore Leicester being on the rocks

indicators.note: some means part of, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

blocks.note: read straight across the words

explanation.surface: Fans lament Leicester City being in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: On the rocks sounds like a football club in crisis; Leicester City is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend the Lorelei is a siren who sits on a rock above the Rhine luring boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: This could be Taylor with Queen, getting more nimble

blocks.note: Taylor Swift, the pop singer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Taylor Swift and a royal get quicker on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This could be' is a by-example signal: Swift is one Taylor among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Swifter is the comparative of swift, meaning quicker or more nimble.

clue.text: Greedy types stealing iron, note – and new and old coins

indicators.note: stealing means taking things into one's possession, so the greedy types hold the following letters

blocks.note: pigs are greedy people
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
n is the dictionary abbreviation for note
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Greedy thieves take iron, a banknote and coins both new and old.
explanation.walkthrough: The pfennig was a small German coin, a hundredth of a mark, before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Pfennigs were the minor currency units of Germany, now out of circulation, so old coins.

clue.text: Study on time in March

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Revising on schedule during the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the study after the time. Capitalised March looks like the month; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to walk with steady steps, as soldiers march.
